title: Explaining a change: the cause chain

p: When something changes, **every reading changes at the same instant**.
The chain is **the order we reason in**, not the order things happen.
Write each step in words. ▲ and ▼ help you read the card; in the exam, write INCREASES or DECREASES.

screens.h: Know what each meter is across
p: Across the battery or the whole external circuit: the **terminal pd**.
Across a series resistor: **I × R**, which moves with the current.
**Brightness is power.** Use P = V²/R or P = I²R for that bulb, with its R constant.

**What changed**: here S closes a new branch.
The **external resistance** of everything outside the box.

screens.q: You are about to write a cause chain. What is step ①?
choices: Say what stays the same: the emf and r.
They belong to the battery and do not change when the circuit changes.
Say that the current increases.
The current is step ④. First say what stays the same.
Write the formula V = IR.
Step ① is what stays the same: the emf and r.
screens.why: Step ① is what stays the same: the emf and r belong to the battery. Then ② what changed, ③ the external resistance, ④ the current, ⑤ the lost volts, ⑥ the terminal pd, ⑦ the part asked.

screens.h: Worked example 11.10: do the headlamps dim?
screens.q: “The circuit below is a simplified diagram of the set-up of the headlamps and starter motor in a car.” (Circuit redrawn: the two headlamps, in parallel, are drawn as one symbol.) “The headlamps are identical. Each headlamp has a constant resistance of 12 Ω and is rated at 55 W. The starter motor has a resistance of 0,05 Ω.” “The battery has an unknown emf and a significant internal resistance r.” “The headlamps are on (switch S₁ is closed).” “The starter motor is then switched on (switch S₂ is closed).” “When both switches are closed, would the brightness of the headlamps INCREASE, STAY THE SAME or DECREASE compared to when only switch S₁ is closed? Briefly explain your answer.” (5)

lines.x: The emf and r stay the same. The starter motor is added in parallel, so the external resistance decreases ✓.

ask.prompt: S₂ adds the motor in parallel. What happens to the external resistance?
choices: INCREASES
A new branch in parallel gives the charge another path, so the external resistance falls.
DECREASES
A new parallel branch is another path, so R_{ext} falls.
STAYS THE SAME
A new branch in parallel gives the charge another path, so the external resistance falls.

lines.x: So the current through the battery increases ✓,

ask.prompt: The emf and r stay the same. What happens to the battery current?
choices: INCREASES
emf = I(R_{ext} + r): a smaller R_{ext} means a larger I.
DECREASES
emf = I(R_{ext} + r) with the emf and r constant: R_{ext} fell, so I rises.
STAYS THE SAME
emf = I(R_{ext} + r) with the emf and r constant: R_{ext} fell, so I rises.

ask.prompt: What happens to the lost volts, Ir?
choices: INCREASES
r is the same and I is larger, so Ir is larger.
DECREASES
r stays the same and I has increased, so Ir increases.
STAYS THE SAME
r stays the same and I has increased, so Ir increases.

lines.x: The terminal pd decreases, and it is the pd across the headlamps ✓.

ask.prompt: What happens to the terminal pd, the pd across the headlamps?
choices: INCREASES
V_{load} = emf − Ir, with the emf constant and Ir larger.
DECREASES
V_{load} = emf − Ir: the emf is the same and Ir is larger.
STAYS THE SAME
V_{load} = emf − Ir, with the emf constant and Ir larger.

lines.x: So the current through each headlamp decreases, and its power, and its brightness, decrease ✓.

ask.prompt: So what happens to the brightness of the headlamps?
choices: INCREASES
The headlamps’ pd fell and their R is constant, so P = V²/R falls.
DECREASES
P = V²/R with the lamp’s R constant and V smaller.
STAYS THE SAME
The headlamps’ pd fell and their R is constant, so P = V²/R falls.

why: “The terminal pd is the pd across the headlamps” ✓. Without it the chain never reaches the lamps ✓.

screens.q: A learner writes: “The internal resistance increases, so the terminal pd decreases.” What is wrong?
choices: r does not change. The current increases, so the lost volts (Ir) increase.
The emf and r stay the same; Ir grows because I grows.
Nothing: that is the memo answer.
This exact slip is in the Examiners’ Report 2019. r belongs to the battery and stays the same.
The terminal pd should increase.
The terminal pd does decrease. The reason is wrong: it is Ir that grows, not r.
screens.why: The current increases, so the lost volts (Ir) increase and the terminal pd decreases. The emf and r stay the same. (IEB Examiners’ Report 2019)

screens.q: A battery (6 V, r = 2 Ω) has two 4 Ω resistors in parallel, with a voltmeter across the battery. A third resistor is connected in parallel. What happens to the voltmeter reading?
choices: INCREASES
Work down the chain: R_{ext} decreases, I increases, Ir increases, so emf − Ir decreases.
DECREASES
R_{ext} falls, I rises, Ir rises, so the terminal pd (emf − Ir) falls.
STAYS THE SAME
Work down the chain: R_{ext} decreases, I increases, Ir increases, so emf − Ir decreases.
screens.why: DECREASE. ① emf and r stay the same; ② a third R in parallel; ③ R_{ext} decreases; ④ I increases; ⑤ Ir increases; ⑥ the terminal pd, which the voltmeter reads, decreases. (IEB 2018 P1 Q7.1.8)
